created_for: mental health real breath VOC literature panels

curation_policy.scope: Human exhaled breath / alveolar gas studies in published literature for psychiatric and neurodevelopmental conditions.
curation_policy.quantified_rule: Numerical log2 fold changes are calculated only from ratios explicitly reported in the cited source.
curation_policy.directional_rule: When a cited source reports only increased/decreased direction for an atlas VOC, measured_log2fc uses conservative placeholder values of +0.6 for increased and -0.4 for decreased, and voc_evidence marks evidence as directional_only.
curation_policy.honesty: Fecal/urine VOC autism studies and unnamed stress-fingerprint VOCs are NOT promoted to measured panels. Anxiety/PTSD/ADHD lack disease-specific named exhaled VOC fold-change cohorts comparable to Magdeburg PTR-MS; those conditions are covered by de-cloned atlas priors with thin-evidence labels, not fake panels.

anxiety.note: Acute psychosocial-stress breath/skin volatilomics exists (Mansour et al. ACS Sensors 2023), but the eight stress VOCs are not named in the abstract and a large e-nose community sample found no generalizable link to clinical anxiety severity.

ptsd.note: Trauma-cue breath odour discrimination (canine proof-of-concept) and acute-stress volatilomics exist, but no named PTSD-vs-control exhaled VOC fold-change panel suitable for atlas measured_log2fc.

adhd.note: No dedicated ADHD case-control exhaled VOC disease panel found. Pediatric executive-function breath pilots are not ADHD diagnostic cohorts and are not copied into measured panels.

autism_spectrum_disorder.note: Published ASD VOC signatures are primarily fecal/urine microbiome volatilomes, not exhaled alveolar gas. Atlas ASD prior remains microbiome-flavored hypothesis, not a breath literature panel.

pentane.note: Phillips et al. reported significantly higher alveolar pentane gradients in schizophrenia vs controls (lipid-peroxidation marker).

ethane.note: Review context in Magdeburg follow-up cites Ross ethane/butane elevation in schizophrenia breath; treated as directional alkane oxidative signal.

carbon_disulfide.note: Phillips et al. reported elevated carbon disulfide alveolar gradients in schizophrenia.

ammonia.note: Cited Popa et al. breath ethylene/ammonia elevation in schizophrenia vs controls (directional only; no fold ratio retained).

acetone.note: Jiang et al. Magdeburg PTR-MS: m/z 59 among 10 masses with reduced concentration in schizophrenia vs controls.

isoprene.note: m/z 69 identified as isoprene; lower in schizophrenia (and MDD) vs healthy controls.

trimethylamine.note: m/z 60 identified as trimethylamine; strongest schizophrenia-vs-control / schizophrenia-vs-MDD discriminator in that cohort.

methanol.note: m/z 33 among masses with significant schizophrenia vs control concentration differences (reduced patient signal in Magdeburg series).

butyric_acid.note: m/z 90 identified as butyric acid / esters; lower in schizophrenia (and MDD) vs healthy controls in Magdeburg PTR-MS cohorts.

supporting_datasets.note: Jiang et al. Magdeburg supplement is a DOCX methods/supplement text dump — not a patient×VOC intensity matrix. No open psych breath intensity cohort bundled.

acetaldehyde.note: Acetaldehyde increased in MDD breath vs controls alongside endogenous ethanol.
